title: The same faces for seven nights
subtitle: A river ship's guest count is fixed. That is either the best part or the worst.

text: There is nowhere to be anonymous on a river ship.
sub: One lounge, one dining room, one sundeck. By the second evening the crew know your name, and so do the other guests. Some travellers love that. Some do not.

left.label: Suits you
items: You want the crew to know you
You travel as a sociable pair

right.label: Doesn't
items: You want a new room nightly
You need range for the family

title: Three things a fixed count changes

items.head: The dining room
items.body: Open seating, one venue, familiar faces. Ask about tables for two if that matters to you.

items.head: The excursion group
items.body: You walk the towns with the same people all week, and the guides learn what the group wants.

items.head: The evenings
items.body: One lounge, conversation, a pianist. Not a theatre, and not a second show at ten.

quote: A hundred guests is a dinner party. Three thousand is a small town. Decide which week you want.

text: Ask the guest count before you ask for the deck plan.
sub: It predicts the social temperature of the week better than any brochure photograph, and it is the one number every line will tell you straight away.

title: Dinner party, or small town?
body: Answer in the comments and I'll say which format I'd put you on — and the two lines I'd start with.
